 Updated Wed, Nov 4 2026 4:16 PM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Dow soars 1,500 points for best day since April 2025 on clear-cut Democratic win, falling oil: Live updates
 Sean Conlon Hugh Leask Traders work on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City. Brendan Mcdermid | Reuters Stocks ripped higher on Wednesday as a decisive victory by Democrats in the U.S. midterm elections — and President Donald Trump's acceptance of the results — removed political uncertainty risk hanging over Wall Street.
 Democrats won majorities in both the House of Representatives and Senate, and scored victories in key gubernatorial races like Texas. The Democrats will now be a check on the policies of Trump, who's enacted business-friendly tax cuts, while also pursuing tariffs and a war in Iran that's boosted inflation.
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 1,569.40 points, or 3.03%, to close at 53,356.12. The 30-stock index moved back above 53,000 for the first time since Sept. 8 and posted its best day since April 9, 2025, when Trump announced a pause on his so-called reciprocal tariffs. The S&P 500 gained 1.58% to end at 7,688.62, while the Nasdaq Composite jumped 1.44% to 25,736.51.
 Stocks extended their gains after U.S. crude oil fell more than 8% as Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for the election losses the Republican party suffered Tuesday. Brent futures traded more than 8% lower as well.
 "There's just going to be even more pressure to end the war," said Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at One Point BFG Wealth Partners. "The American people have obviously expressed their displeasure with inflation and the price of gasoline, amongst other things, and maybe this just pushes for an end to it. We'll have to see."
 Trump told The New York Times he was "absolutely willing" to accept the results and told The Wall Street Journal that he and Republicans would work with Democrats.
 The rebound "was in part due to the president's initial tone and reaction to the results," said Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets. "Still more uncertainty looms, but one thing is certain, there will be gridlock and historically this is good for the market."
 Shares linked to the economy that could benefit from a more stable environment led the gains. Walmart added 3%, while Bank of America rose about 4% as investors looked for stocks outside of technology.
 Heading into the election investors worried a Democratic sweep could weigh on some areas of the market , especially stocks related to the artificial intelligence build-out. Investors feared a big Democratic win could mean more restrictions on data centers nationwide. The Texas governor win by Gina Hinojosa, who's pledged an immediate moratorium in the key data center hub, added to the fears Wednesday. 
 Shares of CoreWeave were lower Wednesday, along with Elon Musk's SpaceX , which is headquartered in Texas. Nvidia also dropped in the session by 3%.
 Another reason for the bullish sentiment Wednesday morning was that history shows the market does well under a divided government , where fewer policies and regulations are able to interfere with the business outlook.
 Andrew Slimmon of Morgan Stanley Investment Management said the markets "like gridlock — they don't like a party with too much power." 
 2 Hours Ago Stocks soar Wednesday
 The three leading U.S. indexes surged on Wednesday.
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 1,569.40 points, or 3.03%, to end the day at 53,356.12, while the S&P 500 added 1.58% to 7,688.62. The Nasdaq Composite gained 1.44% to 25,736.51.
 — Sean Conlon 
 3 Hours Ago Bitcoin rebound lacks new buyer support, says Bitfinex
 Sebastien Bozon | Afp | Getty Images Bitcoin has rebounded after briefly falling to the $75,000 level in the aftermath of the U.S. midterm elections, but the recovery has yet to attract meaningful support from new buyers, according to Bitfinex. It was last trading at about $80,000.
 Analysts at the crypto exchange say gains since Oct. 30 have largely been fueled by short sellers closing their positions , while investors who recently entered the market continue to sell as prices return to their purchase levels. At the same time, outflows from bitcoin ETFs have pushed cumulative net flows for the year into slightly into negative territory, further weakening demand.
 "Sustaining this bounce requires actual spot demand," the report says. "Aggregate bitcoin futures open interest in BTC-notional terms rose to 701,548 BTC on Nov. 3, its highest since Sept. 22. Perpetual funding rates have held close to 11 percent annualized over the past two weeks despite the price correction, while spot buyers have shown little aggression. Together, these readings suggest the bid under $77,000 is primarily underpinned by perpetual futures positions, rather than spot demand."
 — Tanaya Macheel 
 3 Hours Ago Helen of Troy shares surge as it confirms rejection of Empower Brands’ $37-a-share takeover proposal
 Helen of Troy shares jumped about 26% in intraday trading after Empower Brands publicly disclosed its $37-a-share cash takeover proposal. Empower, jointly owned by Spectrum Brands and Oaktree Capital Management, said the proposal implies an enterprise value of approximately $1.6 billion.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Helen of Troy stock price Empower initially offered $34 a share on August 19, which Helen of Troy rejected on September 3. It increased the proposal to $37 on October 12. Helen of Troy's board unanimously rejected the revised proposal on October 20, determining that it significantly undervalued the company, according to the company's investor presentation . 
 The rejection was publicly confirmed today.
 Helen of Troy, whose brands include OXO, Hydro Flask and Osprey, says its standalone strategy offers greater long-term value. It also said Empower declined a nondisclosure agreement that would have allowed access to additional information. Empower characterized the proposed agreement as overly restrictive. 
 "The Company and Board actively engaged with and were responsive to Empower Brands and its advisors, including offering a customary non-disclosure agreement that would allow them to receive information," the company said in a statement. "Empower Brands refused the offer, highlighting the opportunistic nature of the approach and lack of diligence in determining the value of Helen of Troy."
 No deal has been agreed. 
 Helen of Troy maintains that the proposal undervalues its business, but says its board remains open to opportunities that benefit shareholders.
 "The Helen of Troy Board, after comprehensive review alongside its financial and legal advisors, has unanimously determined that Empower Brands' proposal substantially undervalues Helen of Troy and its prospects for continued growth and value creation, and is not in the best interest of Helen of Troy or its shareholders," the Company said in a statement .
 — Deena Zaidi 
 3 Hours Ago Apple surges to record high as investors rethink the AI trade
 The Apple Inc. logo at the company's Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) store during the first day of in-store sales of the iPhone Duo smartphone in Mumbai, India, on Friday, Oct. 23, 2026. Dhiraj Singh | Bloomberg | Getty Images Apple shares rose 6%, reaching an all-time high of $354.33 on Wednesday, pushing the company's market capitalization above $5.12 trillion. The iPhone maker stands to benefit from the sweeping Democratic win , which means slowing data center construction and easing pressure on memory chip prices. Apple has been considered an anti-AI play , with its cautious approach leaving it less exposed to the industry's enormous infrastructure spending.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Apple stock price The company recently posted disappointing margin forecast late Monday and its iPad sales in the fiscal fourth-quarter missed the Street's estimates. Apple had blamed higher memory prices and some costs related to Siri AI for the shrinking margins. 
 But the stock could now be an early winner from the Democratic mid term victory.
 — Deena Zaidi 
 4 Hours Ago Why a Democratic landslide would continue to weigh on the U.S. dollar
 Stopwatch on the US dollars. Baona | Istock | Getty Images The most important policy implication of a Democratic landslide in the U.S. midterm election is a prospective slowdown of data-center construction, according to Thierry Wizman, Global FX & Rates Strategist at Macquarie Group.
 He said that because AI infrastructure investment has supported U.S. growth, "any politically driven slowdown would be adverse for the U.S. dollar ." 
 Wizman identified this as one of the three most important medium-term dollar drivers, alongside oil/war and European debt sustainability. The ICE U.S. Dollar Index dropped Wednesday after Democrats flipped Senate and House in stunning victory, removing uncertainty for markets.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon ICE U.S. Dollar Index — Deena Zaidi 
 5 Hours Ago Blue wave creates crypto challenges and banking sector uncertainty, says Compass Point
 watch now VIDEO 4:51 04:51 Wall Street reacts to the midterm election results Rapid Recap Democrats strong showing Tuesday night could create a challenging regulatory environment for the financial services and crypto industries.
 Investors should expect Elizabeth Warren to chair the Senate Banking Committee, where her opposition to crypto is likely to stall supportive crypto legislation, including the Clarity Act, Compass Point analyst Ed Groshans said in a note Wednesday. Instead, Cryptoasset adoption will largely depend on SEC and CFTC regulatory actions.
 "Warren is opposed to cryptoassets," he said." She has sought amendments to limit tokenization … does not support the regulatory approval of perpetual futures. We do not expect the SBC to act on any legislative efforts, such as the Clarity Act, to broaden cryptoasset adoption with Warren as Chair.
 Groshans also said the banking sector should anticipate increased political and headline risk, particularly around Basel III revisions. He sees the greatest opportunities for financial services legislation are capping consumer interest rates at 36% and addressing credit card interchange.
 — Tanaya Macheel 
 5 Hours Ago CoreWeave credit default swaps move higher
 Jonathan Raa | Nurphoto | Getty Images Spreads on CoreWeave 's five-year credit default swaps moved 3% higher on Wednesday to 1,139.7 after the election created more hurdles for data center plays. 
 Credit default swaps are contracts where buyers pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. The spread widening in CoreWeave's CDS means investors view the debt as riskier. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 also ticked 3 basis points higher to 15.919%. One basis point is equal to 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions.
 CoreWeave's five-year credit default swaps Democrats, seen as friendlier to data center restrictions, had resounding wins across the country, including in Texas -- where the newly elected governor has said she wants an immediate moratorium on data centers in the state. Ballot measures on their development were also shot down in various states. 
 CoreWeave has been trading above 1,000 in recent weeks as investors became more concerned about the debt being taken on to fund artificial intelligence infrastructure. That level is generally seen as signaling distress.
 — Michelle Fox 
 6 Hours Ago Sluggish traffic gives McDonald's its first U.S. same-store sales decline in a year and a half
 McDonald's shares rising modestly after better-than-expected third quarter earnings. The rally is also a reflection that "less bad" is outweighing "less good" on the sales front.
 Although U.S. same-store sales fell for the first time in 6 quarters, but the 0.2% decline was less than the 0.5% that Wall Street expected. Although traffic was down in July and August, trends improved in September, providing some optimism going forward.
 It was a very different story abroad though. International restaurants saw positive sales growth, more than offsetting the domestic sales decline. Same-store sales for International Operated Markets rose 1.4%, driving the rather mundane 1.5% growth across the entire company. But despite that strength in overseas sales, the rise was a disappointment since it was less than the 2.1% projected by analysts.
 — Robert Hum 
 8 Hours Ago Communication services ETF heading for best day since April 2025
 Shares of the State Street Communication Services Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLC) were up nearly 4% on Wednesday, pacing for its best day since April 2025. 
 Top holdings of the XLC were higher across the board. Alphabet was up nearly 5%, as was the Walt Disney Company, and Meta Platforms was higher by almost 2%. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon State Street Communication services Select Sector SPDR ETF 1-day. — Davis Giangiulio 
 8 Hours Ago Magnificent Seven stocks buck the trend 
 Jakub Porzycki | Nurphoto | Getty Images Magnificent Seven stocks rallied Wednesday morning, breaking away from the broader artificial intelligence trade that was in a downturn. 
 Apple up 6%
 Amazon up 7% 
 Alphabet up 5% 
 Meta Platforms up 2% 
 Microsoft up 6% 
 The two exceptions were Elon Musk's Tesla, which slid 2%, and Nvidia, which was lower by 1%.
 The AI trade more broadly was selling off, as investors dumped shares of the companies most likely to get hurt by greater scrutiny from a left-leaning Congress. Semiconductors fell 1%, as shown by the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX). And, neocloud stocks dropped 6%, according to the Roundhill Neocloud ETF (NCLD). 
 Shares of Coreweave dropped more than 7%, while Nebius fell more than 4%. 
 — Sarah Min 
 9 Hours Ago Consumer staples ETF hits all-time high
 A person shops at a Dollar General store on May 28, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois. Scott Olson | Getty Images The State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLP) hit a fresh all-time record on Wednesday morning.
 The fund, which was last up more than 2%, was led higher by gains in Dollar Tree , Constellation Brands , Estee Lauder , Doller General and Conagra Brands , among others.
 XLP is on pace to finish the year with solid gains, having risen about 17% in the period.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon XLP, year-to-date — Gina Francolla and Sean Conlon 
 9 Hours Ago Stocks surge to start Wednesday's session
 U.S. equities jumped at the beginning of Wednesday trading.
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average rocketed higher by 1,022 points, or 2%, just after the opening bell, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite each added 1.3%. 
 — Sean Conlon 
 10 Hours Ago Trump media among the stocks making moves premarket
 Here are some of the names moving before the opening bell: 
 Trump Media & Technology Group — Shares of President Donald Trump 's social media company and tech company were down 11% after a decisive victory by Democrats in the U.S. midterm elections Tuesday night. Trump owns 41% of the company, which owns social media platform Truth Social. Democrats taking control of Congress adds a check on the president's policies.
 Neocloud stocks — So-called neocloud companies moved lower after the election, with CoreWeave dropping 8% and Iren and Nebius both shedding 6%. The Democratic wins in Texas and rejection of data centers in ballots across the country is expected to create hurdles for data center plays. 
 McDonald's — The fast-food restaurant chain reported mixed quarterly results , sending shares 2% higher. Adjusted earnings came in at $3.57 per share, topping the $3.38 expected from analysts polled by LSEG. However, its revenue of $7.16 billion fell short of the $7.29 billion consensus estimate. 
 To see the full list of movers, click here .
 — Michelle Fox and Paulina Likos 
 10 Hours Ago Private companies added 86,000 jobs in October, ADP says
 SUNRISE, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 25: Vincent Pinzone of Life Alert speaks with people about job opportunities during the Mega JobNewsUSA South Florida Job Fair at Amerant Bank Arena on September 25, 2026, in Sunrise, Florida. Hiring managers and recruiters from more than 50 companies attended the job fair to recruit workers for opportunities across a range of companies. (Photo by Joe Raedle/Getty Images) Joe Raedle | Getty Images News | Getty Images Private-sector job growth held steady in October, with gains spread across sectors, as the labor market showed fresh signs of stabilization, ADP reported Wednesday.
 The payrolls processing firm said companies added 86,000 jobs during the month, the same as the downwardly revised total for September and slightly ahead of the Dow Jones estimate for 75,000.
 Read the full story here .
 — Jeff Cox 
 13 Hours Ago Huge reversal in Nasdaq-100 futures
 Nasdaq-100 futures are up 929.75 points off their overnight lows, based on the current price of 28,545.50. Futures contracts tied to the benchmark hit a low of 27,615.75,  their lowest since July 30.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Nasdaq-100 futures in past months — Gina Francolla 
 13 Hours Ago Precious metals rise as Democrats take control of Congress
 Gold rose on Tuesday, as safe-haven demand lingered amid geopolitical uncertainty, while silver also hovered near all-time highs. Ravitaliy | Istock | Getty Images Precious metals saw strong gains on Wednesday morning as the Democrats scored a clean sweep in the midterm elections, flipping both the House and Senate.
 Spot gold was 2.93% higher at $4,043.45 an ounce by 5:05 a.m. ET, while spot silver jumped 4.44% to trade at $51.98 per ounce, as traders reacted to the U.S. midterm election results.
 Front-month gold futures added 2.9% to trade at $4,054.60, while silver futures were up 4.64% at $52.09.
 Other metals seeing notable gains on Wednesday morning included platinum , which jumped 2.47% to trade at $1,465.30, and palladium, which was 5.93% higher at $989.
 — Chloe Taylor 
 14 Hours Ago Renewables and health stocks rally as Democrats take Congress
 Renewables and healthcare shares are among the biggest premarket movers, trading higher after Democrats took control of the House and Senate. Meanwhile, neocloud stocks, as well as prison operators and defense names, lag the broader market.
 U.S. renewable energy stocks climbed on expectations of a policy shift. First Solar advanced 8.5%, Bloom Energy gained 5.8%, Plug Power rose 10.6%, Sunrun notched an 8.64% gain, FuelCell Energy was up 6.24% and SolarEdge Technologies moved 4% higher.
 Healthcare stocks also rose. UnitedHealth gained 1.8%, Molina Healthcare added 6.3%, Centene climbed 5% and HCA Healthcare advanced 7.16%.
 Neocloud stocks, in contrast, turned lower, with CoreWeave down 3.6% and Nebius off 1%. Shares of prison operators and defense names also fell.
 — Hugh Leask 
 15 Hours Ago European renewables stocks surge on projected Democrat win
 A Vestas wind turbine photographed in April 2022. Karol Serewis/Sopa Images | Lightrocket | Getty Images European renewable energy stocks moved sharply higher in early trade as prospects of a decisive Democrat victory in the U.S. midterm elections sparked hopes of a U.S. policy shift on renewables.
 Copenhagen-listed Oersted surged 7.3% while Danish peer Vestas advanced 5.2%. The two companies have grappled with uncertainty in their U.S. businesses in recent years, partly as a result of fierce opposition from the Trump administration toward the renewable energy sector.
 SMA Solar shares were up 5.5% and Nordex shares added 4.8%. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Oersted. — Hugh Leask 
 15 Hours Ago European stock markets open in the green
 The pan-European Stoxx 600 added 0.44% in early trading, as the continent's stocks and major bourses moved higher on the Democrats' clean sweep of the U.S. midterms.
 Banks advanced 1.83%, leading gains, with basic resources up 1.71% and utilities rising 0.68%. Food and beverage stocks lost 0.57%, and industrial goods fell 0.37%.
 The Italian FTSE MIB was up 0.88%, leading regional bourses. The U.K.'s FTSE 100 added 0.22%, while the French CAC 40 rose 0.24% and Germany's DAX gained 0.28%.
 — Hugh Leask 
 15 Hours Ago Novo shares jump after earnings beat, outlook hike
 Novo posted quarterly earnings ahead of expectations early Wednesday as sales of its Wegovy pill blew past estimates amid continued GLP-1 volume growth globally, sending shares up as much as 6% in early trading.
 The company updated its outlook to now see adjusted revenue and operating profit growth between negative 2% and 2% at constant exchange rates. It previously saw full-year sales and operating profits, which it hiked in August, at negative 6% to flat for both metrics.
 Sales in the third quarter came in at 79.2 billion Danish kroner ($11.9 billion), up 4% year-on-year at constant exchange rates and ahead of FactSet estimates of 73.6 billion kroner. Adjusted operating profit (EBIT) was 31.7 billion kroner, compared with the expected 28.6 billion kroner.
 It comes as the Danish weight-loss drug maker is looking to regain momentum following a tumultuous year in which it fell behind rival Eli Lilly. 
 Read more here . 
 — Elsa Ohlen 
 16 Hours Ago Asia markets close mixed in choppy trading 
 Asia-Pacific markets closed mixed Wednesday, as investors assessed a projected Democratic takeover of the U.S. Senate and House, while President Donald Trump appeared to not challenge the results.
 "We'll work with the Democrats, and we'll get along very well with them," Trump told the Wall Street Journal. 
 South Korea's Kospi rose 0.62% to end at 5,683.8, while the small-cap, tech-focused Kosdaq added 1.5% to 714.95 in choppy trading.
 Japan's  Nikkei 225 pared some losses to close 1.42% lower at 62,188.63, and the broad-based Topix declined 0.89% to 3,895.38.
 Mainland China's CSI 300 gained 2.31% to 4,101.34, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was 1.43% higher in its last hour of trade.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.59% to 8,834.5.
 — Lee Ying Shan and Lim Hui Jie 
 16 Hours Ago Dollar slides as Democrats take control of Congress 
 The dollar and other major currencies were in a holding pattern on Monday as investors turned their attention to this week's US midterm elections, which could shift the balance of power in Congress and control over the federal purse strings. Sheldon Cooper | Lightrocket | Getty Images The dollar moved lower against most major currencies as the Democrats took control of Congress after the U.S. midterm elections.
 The euro was last seen 0.39% higher against the dollar at $1.1235, while the British pound also strengthened against the greenback, rising 0.48% to $1.3476.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Dollar Index. The dollar index , which tracks the greenback's strength against a basket of six major currencies, was down 0.39% at $101.32.
 — Hugh Leask 
 17 Hours Ago Treasury yields fall as Democrat midterm wins continue to pile up 
 Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) during morning trading on Aug. 24, 2026 in New York City. Angela Weiss | AFP | Getty Images Treasury yields moved lower on Wednesday as investors sought shelter from a sell-off in equity futures sparked by potential big victories from Democrats in the U.S. midterm elections.
 The benchmark 10-year Treasury note yield was last seen 1 basis point lower at 4.9311%. The 30-year bond yield slipped 1 basis point to 5.3136%, and the shorter-term 2-year note yield pulled back 1 basis point to 4.6017%.
 — Hugh Leask 
 17 Hours Ago European stock futures lower with Democrats set to sweep U.S. midterms
 European stock markets are set to open negative as investors respond to overnight projections of a major Democratic victory in the U.S. midterms.
 The Democrats are projected to win both chambers of Congress, according to The Associated Press.
 Stoxx 50 futures were lower by 0.35% ahead of Wednesday's market open.
 Futures tied to the U.K.'s FTSE 100 were 0.64% lower, with Germany's DAX off by 0.46%. France's CAC 40 is set to start the session 0.28% lower, while Italy's FTSE MIB is down 0.21%.
 — Hugh Leask 
 19 Hours Ago Asia chip stocks tumble as Democrats flip Senate after winning House
 Asian semiconductor stocks tumbled Wednesday as Democrats are projected to win both the House and the Senate in the U.S. midterm elections.
 That has stoked worries over curbs on AI infrastructure buildout at a time when AI-linked stocks have been declining on concerns about weaker spending.
 Japan's Softbank Group plunged over 8%, while chipmaking equipment company Disco fell 10.19%. Advantest shed over 8% and Renesas Electronics declined 7.64%. Tokyo Electron was down 7.04%.
 South Korean chip heavyweights also came under pressure, with SK Hynix dropping 5.08% and Samsung Electronics declining 3.87%. Seoul Semiconductor shed 4.37%.
 Taiwanese chipmaking giant TSMC slipped 1.09%.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 19 Hours Ago Trump Media & Technology shares drop as Democratic sweep seems more likely
 Cheng Xin | Getty Images Shares of Trump Media & Technology declined more than 7% in overnight trading on Robinhood as the 2026 midterm elections appear poised to conclude with a blue wave.
 The stock moved lower after CNBC's Election Desk projected that Democrats are going to win the House. The party was also on track to take Senate control from Republicans.
 President Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post late Tuesday, "I wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!"
 — Sean Conlon 
 20 Hours Ago Japan's Nikkei plunges over 4% to lowest since May as U.S. midterm election jitters rattle AI stocks
 The Nikkei 225 Stock Average displayed inside the Kabuto One building in Tokyo, Japan, on Monday, Oct. 26, 2026. Kiyoshi Ota | Bloomberg | Getty Images Japan's Nikkei 225 plunged more than 4% on Wednesday, leading losses across Asia-Pacific markets as renewed jitters over artificial intelligence stocks weighed on investor sentiment amid uncertainty surrounding the U.S. midterm elections.
 The benchmark declined 4.45% to its lowest since May. Technology and energy stocks led declines in the benchmark, according to data from LSEG, while the broader Topix index tumbled more than 3%. 
 The sell-off came as investors weighed the prospect of tighter restrictions on data-center development under a potential Democratic-controlled Congress, adding to concerns over the outlook for AI-related spending.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 20 Hours Ago Treasury yields slide
 Treasury yields fell as investors sought shelter from a sell-off in equity futures sparked by potential big victories from Democrats in the U.S. midterm elections.
 The benchmark 10-year Treasury note yield dropped nearly 5 basis points to 4.902%. The 30-year bond yield slid 5.29%, and the shorter-term 2-year note yield pulled back 6 basis points to 4.55%. Read more .
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon US10Y, 1-day — Fred Imbert 
 20 Hours Ago SpaceX shares fall as Hinojosa continues lead in Texas governor election
 Nikolas Kokovlis | Nurphoto | Getty Images Shares of SpaceX fell more than 6% on Robinhood overnight trading as Democratic candidate Gina Hinojosa continued her lead over Republican incumbent Greg Abbott in the Texas gubernatorial race.
 "Let's watch SpaceX. Let's watch Tesla . This is Elon Musk-land now. There are a lot of California companies that moved to Texas, thinking, 'All right, we're going to get out of this blue state and go somewhere safe,' and now it's proven that it isn't," Jay Woods, Freedom Capital Markets' chief market strategist, said in an interview with CNBC.
 "You want to watch a lot of these Texas companies that moved there," he stressed.
 Musk said that he was going to move the headquarters of both companies to Texas from California back in 2024. Tesla shares were down more than 4% on Robinhood.
 — Sean Conlon 
 21 Hours Ago Investors watching Texas for AI trade clues
 Investors were focusing on the results of the Texas gubernatorial race for clues about the AI trade because the state represents an outsized portion of data center capacity. Democratic candidate Gina Hinojosa has an early lead over Republican incumbent Greg Abbott. Hinojosa is calling for an immediate moratorium on data centers in the state and an end any tax incentives for the build-out.
 "The one thing that could really end up moving stuff though would be if Abbott were to lose Texas," said Scott Ladner, chief investment officer of Horizon Investments. "Because there is a legitimate question about, where do you build these data centers?"
 "Texas is a fertile ground for that. And if he were to lose, I think that fertile ground is largely barren. So, that's going to be a challenge. And so the AI trade — at least for next couple days — does hinge on does Abbott win or not," Ladner added. 
 Texas represents about 27% of U.S. data center gigawatts, estimates Wells Fargo.
 — John Melloy and Sarah Min 
 22 Hours Ago Volatility spurred by the midterms could be an opportunity for investors, strategist says
 People vote at a polling location on Election Day during the midterm elections in New York City on November 3, 2026. Timothy A. Clary | Afp | Getty Images Any big surprises out of the 2026 midterm elections could mean buying opportunities for investors, according to Angelo Kourkafas, senior strategist at Edward Jones.
 "The results could act as a clearing event removing some uncertainty, though developments around the AI theme and geopolitics are the primary forces driving markets heading into the final two months of the year," he said.
 However, he added: "If we do see election-driven volatility it may present an opportunity for long-term investors to lean into it."
 — Sean Conlon 
 22 Hours Ago HSBC issues $4.25 billion in two-part debt offering
 HSBC said on Wednesday it had issued $4.25 billion in senior unsecured debt in two tranches, including $1.75 billion in notes due in 2032 at 5.819% fixed-rate/floating-rate and another $2.5 billion in notes maturing in 2037 at 6.262%. 
 Europe's largest bank, which plans to list the securities on the New York Stock Exchange, did not specify how the funds raised would be deployed.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 22 Hours Ago VIX futures rise above 20
 Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) futures moved higher on Tuesday evening as U.S. equity futures came under pressure amid results from the midterm elections.
 Futures tied to the VIX, otherwise referred to as Wall Street's " fear gauge ," were last seen trading at 20.90.
 A move above 20 tends to be a key level signaling heightened angst among investors in the market.
 — Sean Conlon 
 23 Hours Ago How the S&P 500 has performed after midterms
 Investors are on edge as polls across the U.S. begin closing in an election that could bring gridlock to government. But if history is any indication, they may have little to worry about. 
 A CNBC analysis of S&P 500 returns after elections from 1980 through 2024 shows the benchmark rose an average of 0.2% one day after the election and 1.1% in the month following. One year out, the benchmark averages a 13.8% return and rose in 91% of cases. That's including general elections. 
 Looking at just post-midterm returns, the record is even stronger. The S&P 500 has risen after each of the last 11 midterm elections between 1982 and 2022. One year out, the index returns 13.7% on average. 
 Read the full story here .
 — Deena Zaidi and Nick Wells 
 23 Hours Ago Solar ETF extends gains in after hours trading
 watch now VIDEO 1:03 01:03 Options Action: Bulls take a shine to solar stocks Options Action The Invesco Solar ETF (TAN) rose by 1.3% in after hours trading on Tuesday, extending gains from the regular session when the ETF rallied 3% as traders bet on stocks most likely to benefit from Democrat leadership. 
 Options trading in solar companies surged Tuesday, following a five-month selloff for the group. Volume in the Invesco Solar ETF (TAN) surged to 40 times higher than usual, according to Cboe LiveVol data. The fund, which typically trades fewer than 500 contracts a day the past month, traded more than 20,000 contracts by midday, and 99% of them were calls. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon TAN, 1-day — Sarah Min and Oliver Renick 
 23 Hours Ago Chip stocks give up gains
 Shares of key chipmakers gave up their initial gains on Tuesday evening, moving into negative territory.

 24 Hours Ago CVS Health rises on WSJ report that it will split off its retail pharmacy business
 CVS Health Corp. signage on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, US, on Monday, July 28, 2025.  Tue, Nov 3 2026 6:24 PM EST Stocks making the biggest moves after hours: AMD, Super Micro & more
 Lisa Su, chair and chief executive officer of Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD), speaks during the company's Gamers Day event in Seoul, South Korea, on Wednesday, Oct. 7, 2026. SeongJoon Cho | Bloomberg | Getty Images A slate of stocks moved sharply in extended trading, largely driven by the latest earnings reports: 
 Advanced Micro Devices — The chipmaker jumped 7% after reporting stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings . Adjusted earnings of $2.09 per share topped estimates for $1.95, according to analysts polled by LSEG. Revenue forecasts for the current quarter also came in above estimates
 Super Micro Computer — Shares of the server company jumped more than 9% after Super Micro earnings per share and revenue beat Wall Street estimates. For fiscal year 2027, the company expects net sales to range between $72 billion and $82 billion, above the LSEG consensus for $69.17 billion.
 Arista Networks — The cloud networking company gained 12% after current-quarter guidance topped estimates. Arista sees fourth-quarter earnings of $1.26 to $1.30 per share on revenue of $3.9 billion to $4.0 billion. Analysts surveyed by LSEG were looking for $1.15 per share and $3.60 billion.
 Read more about Tuesday's movers in extended trading here .
 — Darla Mercado
